answers.answer: Scheduler.start() (scheduler.py:107-122) binds or creates the run, then calls _plan_all_routes() (line 120) before dispatcher reconciliation. _plan_all_routes builds the M2 request from every entry in self.plan.tasks, including dependencies, acceptance criteria and verification, with no state filter (lines 130-137). Blocked and PENDING tasks are therefore included. The READY filter exists only in _assign's eligible() (scheduler.py:295-297), which is the execution-time path. The core test asserts that T1, T2 and T3 are all sent to M2 and that the dependent T2 stays 'pending' (test_routing.py:53-68).

One batch operation for the map. The bridge is SchedulerCore._plan_all_routes calling port.plan (scheduler.py:141), implemented by DecisionAssignmentPort.plan (bt_scheduler_adapter.py:340-345), which delegates to plan_full_dag. plan_full_dag builds one DecisionRequest per task (per-task candidates and evidence, lines 160-180), then calls port.ledger.batch_decisions.persist once with all requests (lines 182-188). The joint allocation happens in plan_ready_batch and _match_batch_routes, an augmenting-path matching over all tasks; the plan path sets free_slots to len(tasks) (line 172). This path does not call engine.decide, so there is no per-task decision.

Two stores. (a) The Scheduler RunState keeps route_metadata, route_status and route_reason on each TaskRec and routing_complete on RunState (model.py:29-31, 79). These are serialized in to_dict (model.py:97, with tasks via vars at line 100) and validated in from_dict (model.py:111-130). _plan_all_routes writes them in persist (scheduler.py:156-173). (b) The M2 batch is stored immutably in the batch_decisions table (batch_ledger.py:240-299). Restart protection: start() calls _plan_all_routes again, which returns early when routing_complete is set (scheduler.py:127), and persist re-checks that flag (line 157). Tasks that already have attempts are skipped (lines 162-163). An identical batch input replays the stored result (batch_ledger.py:273-282). The repository's storage medium and write atomicity were not inspected.

No. Whole-plan mapping does not reserve executor capacity or launch work. The only reservation is reservation.claim (lines 34-71), reached via SchedulerCore.claim (scheduler.py:229-231) from _assign (line 325). The plan path writes only route fields and the routing_complete flag in the RunState (scheduler.py:156-173), plus a durable but non-capacity batch_decisions row. The adapter docstring says 'without reserving capacity' (bt_scheduler_adapter.py:341). The integration test patches engine.decide to raise and asserts zero decision_records rows and one batch (test_scheduler_decision_integration.py:214-248). One caveat: batch.py:375 says 'without creating durable reservations', but the batch row is durable audit data, not a capacity hold.

Not blindly reused. _assign's eligible() builds an AssignmentRequest from READY tasks only, and its TaskView carries spec data and the attempt count, not the planned route (scheduler.py:295-307). DecisionAssignmentPort.propose refreshes quota again (adapter line 357), recomputes requested_at (361), rebuilds candidates from _candidate_rows (371), marks candidates from non-available preflight profiles as unknown (372-380), persists a new batch (396-399), and runs engine.decide on the selected assignment (410). claim then overwrites route_metadata and sets route_status to 'assigned' (reservation.py:54-56). The integration test shows the initial plan choosing a profile other than codex-luis, then a changed quota at step() leading to a claim on codex-luis (test lines 401-445). Caveat: the planned route stays visible in the snapshot until a successful claim.

Conversion happens at several points. In refresh(): a poll exception sets poll_failed (bt_scheduler_quota_preflight.py:35-40), which yields refresh_failed (59-60). Other statuses map to malformed, stale, refresh_failed or missing (61-75). An item is 'available' only when fresh (76-80). Antigravity errors fail closed (100-101). Account-limit overflow returns a '*' sentinel (28-29). In plan_full_dag, a refresh exception becomes a '*' sentinel (bt_scheduler_plan_routing.py:147-150). _apply_preflight marks any non-available candidate as unknown (63-73), and _quota_evidence maps reasons to states (76-109). Timestamps: quota_aware_requested_at (29-38) is evaluated after the refresh and returns the max of request.now, time.time() at that moment, and every finite observed_at in the result. The planning and ready paths both call it (lines 151 and adapter 361). Caveat: it does not filter by status, so a non-fresh row with a future observed_at still moves requested_at. It uses time.time(), not the injected clock. Tests assert requested_at >= observed_at for a fresh injected observation (test_scheduler_decision_integration.py:284-310, 312-335) and fail-closed refresh_failed evidence (267-282).

The best integration test is test_ready_revalidation_uses_changed_quota_and_m1_owns_the_only_reservation (test_scheduler_decision_integration.py:401-445). Scenario: a frozen REQ-017 task. Quota starts with claude-personal available and codex-luis unavailable. A direct port.plan call (line 427) produces a route that is not codex-luis (line 437). The SchedulerCore is built with Ports(assignment=port) and no routing port, so start() does not remap (lines 428-432). The task becomes READY, quota changes (434), and step() refreshes again (refresh_calls asserted at 438). It makes exactly one claim (439-442) that resolves via ledger lookup to codex-luis, gpt-6.1-sol, high (443-445). The core stub test test_routing.py:53-80 separately asserts a plan route of sonnet being replaced by a haiku ready route, with no executor. Its M2 is a stub, not the real adapter.

unknowns: Repository implementation (StateRepository transaction durability and file or database storage) was not inspected, so write atomicity between RunState route fields and the batch ledger is unverified.

Production wiring: bt_scheduler_run.py:41-45 passes the DecisionAssignmentPort through composition.wire, and bt_scheduler_executor_wiring.py:82-83 passes it as routing when it has a callable plan. The intermediate hop was not fully traced.
Account-capacity defaults in _account_capacities and the route policy internals were not traced in depth.
The integration test starts the scheduler without a routing port, so it does not exercise start-time plan mapping together with a READY revalidation in one run.
Freshness thresholds depend on bt_subscriptions.MAX_AGE_SECONDS and bt_agy.MAX_AGE_SEC, which were not inspected.
No test was executed; all test statements are source assertions only, and no check is claimed to have passed.
